contentNote: 320 original practice questions. Related reading provides context; questions are not copied from or endorsed by the linked providers. Recall is self-assessed. Employer role mappings are study recommendations inferred from each company’s work, not verified job requirements.

sources.title: UBCx · Silicon Photonics Design, Fabrication and Data Analysis
sources.description: Hands-on modeling, mask layout, fabrication and measured data analysis. A strong bridge from optics into PIC work. Instructor-paced; check current enrollment and fabrication arrangements.

sources.title: AIM Photonics · Online courses
sources.description: Focused modules in fundamentals, passive test, active test, detectors and modulators, simulation, and sensing. Check registration, pricing and prerequisites on the provider site.

sources.title: MIT Microphotonics · Teaching packages
sources.description: Integrated silicon photonics and photonic materials/device teaching packages. Useful structured background alongside device exercises.

sources.title: Southampton · Silicon Photonics OPTO6007
sources.description: A university module covering guided waves, passive and active devices, fabrication and integration. Use as a syllabus reference; public listing does not imply open remote enrollment.

sources.title: ePIXfab · Training catalog
sources.description: Specialist silicon photonics training, schools and workshops. Mostly event-based; location, availability and dates vary.

sources.title: Ansys Optics · Learning and device examples
sources.description: Official solver tutorials and device workflows. Commercial software access may be needed to run examples.

sources.title: Ansys · Finite-difference eigenmode solver
sources.description: Mode profiles, effective index, loss, dispersion and convergence.

sources.title: Ansys · Ring modulator workflow
sources.description: Device-level extraction and circuit assembly for rings and racetracks.

sources.title: Ansys · Traveling-wave Mach–Zehnder modulator
sources.description: Electro-optic modeling, traveling-wave electrodes and high-speed response.

sources.title: Ansys · PIN Mach–Zehnder modulator
sources.description: Carrier distributions, index perturbations and modulation.

sources.title: Ansys · Germanium-on-silicon photodetector
sources.description: Optical absorption, electrical collection and detector performance modeling.

sources.title: Ansys · Electro-absorption modulator
sources.description: GeSi electro-absorption modeling on an SOI platform.

sources.title: Ansys · Grating coupler
sources.description: Fiber overlap, geometry optimization and coupling simulation.

sources.title: Ansys · Y branch
sources.description: Passive splitting, complex scattering parameters and circuit models.

sources.title: GDSFactory · Documentation
sources.description: Python-based layout, ports, routing, PDKs, hierarchy and verification workflows. Generic examples do not authorize foundry fabrication.

sources.title: AIM Photonics · Low-loss PDK
sources.description: Example of a foundry stack combining silicon, SiN, implants, germanium detection and metal layers.

sources.title: AIM Photonics · PDK agreements
sources.description: Access and development/commercialization terms. Check the current agreement before planning a tape-out.

sources.title: Shekhar et al. · Roadmapping the Next Generation of Silicon Photonics
sources.description: A field-wide perspective on devices, circuits, fabrication, integration and packaging. Read critically: a roadmap is not a production guarantee.

sources.title: Foundry perspective on laser and SOA integration
sources.description: Integration approaches and challenges for silicon photonics light sources.

sources.title: Advances in silicon quantum photonics
sources.description: Review of integrated quantum photonic devices and scaling challenges.

sources.title: Intel · Silicon photonics
sources.description: Optical I/O, PIC/EIC integration, lasers and system architecture. Vendor claims need their stated operating conditions.

sources.title: Broadcom · Co-packaged optics
sources.description: CPO switch architectures, optical engines and external laser sources.

sources.title: NVIDIA · Silicon photonics networking
sources.description: CPO in AI networking; useful context for system and packaging priorities.

sources.title: ANELLO · Silicon photonic gyroscopes
sources.description: Integrated optical gyroscopes and navigation applications beyond datacom.

sources.title: Photonics Spectra
sources.description: Industry reporting, component/application articles, webinars and workforce coverage. Start with integrated photonics and test topics.

sources.title: Laser Focus World
sources.description: Photonics technologies, lasers, optics and test; newsletters, webinars and industry context.

sources.title: Lightwave
sources.description: Optical communications, data-center networks, transceivers and deployment context.

sources.title: Journal of Lightwave Technology
sources.description: Peer-reviewed optical communication, devices and system papers. Access varies by article and subscription.

sources.title: OFC · Optical Fiber Communication Conference
sources.description: Conference papers, technical program, short courses and industry networking. Verify the next event catalog before booking.

sources.title: SPIE Photonics West
sources.description: San Francisco industry event, technical conferences and courses. Check current course offerings and registration.

topics.objectives: Compare platform choices; connect PIC and EIC functions; understand foundry access.

topics.title: Waveguides & modes
topics.subtitle: Confinement, dispersion, propagation loss and bends.
topics.objectives: Compute phase and delay; inspect supported modes; assess geometry sensitivity.

topics.title: Passive building blocks
topics.subtitle: Couplers, splitters, crossings, Bragg gratings and AWGs.
topics.objectives: Interpret scattering matrices; balance loss and tolerance; select passive topologies.

topics.title: Interferometers
topics.subtitle: Mach–Zehnder transfer functions, phase and bias.
topics.objectives: Calculate phase and FSR; reason about extinction; calibrate quadrature.

topics.title: Rings & resonators
topics.subtitle: FSR, Q, coupling regimes and thermal locking.

topics.title: Getting light on chip

topics.objectives: Compare interfaces; calculate coupling loss; evaluate assembly tolerances.

topics.title: High-speed modulation

questions.prompt: What makes SOI useful for tightly confined photonic waveguides?
answers: High index contrast between silicon and oxide
options: High index contrast between silicon and oxide
questions.explanation: The oxide undercladding confines light; high contrast enables compact bends but increases geometry sensitivity.

questions.prompt: SOI stands for silicon on ___.
questions.explanation: A thin silicon device layer sits above a buried insulating oxide.

questions.prompt: Explain why a silicon waveguide is not automatically a useful laser.
answers: Bulk silicon has an indirect bandgap; efficient gain usually comes from an added active material.
questions.explanation: Momentum conservation suppresses efficient radiative recombination. Guiding and generating light are different functions.

questions.prompt: Which material commonly provides telecom photodetection on silicon?
questions.explanation: Germanium absorbs telecom light that silicon guides with relatively little intrinsic absorption.

questions.prompt: Compare silicon and silicon nitride for a long passive delay line.
answers: SiN can offer lower propagation loss and lower nonlinearity, often with larger bends and no native silicon junction modulation.
questions.explanation: Actual performance depends on the foundry stack and cross section, not the material name alone.

questions.prompt: A PIC manipulates light; an EIC primarily processes ___ signals.
questions.explanation: PIC and EIC functions must be co-designed for drivers, receivers, control, and power.

questions.prompt: Select functions normally assigned to an EIC in an optical transceiver.
questions.explanation: Electronics drive the optical modulator and convert detector current into a useful voltage.

questions.prompt: Why is CMOS compatibility useful but insufficient for a photonics product?
answers: It enables scalable fabrication, but optical materials, packaging, testing, and yield still require specialized engineering.
questions.explanation: A compatible process does not automatically solve laser integration or fiber attachment.

questions.prompt: What does an MPW service share between participating designs?
questions.explanation: Multiple designs share mask and fabrication costs; each must obey the selected process rules.

questions.prompt: Why might a platform offer both silicon and SiN waveguides?
answers: Silicon supports compact active components; SiN supports low-loss passive routing and broader spectral use.
questions.explanation: Interlayer transitions add design constraints and loss that belong in the link budget.

questions.prompt: A foundry PDK is a process ___ kit.
questions.explanation: It connects layout layers, rules, characterized components, and models to a fabrication process.

questions.prompt: Which criterion best selects a platform for a product?
answers: Required functions, loss, manufacturability, and packaging compatibility
options: Required functions, loss, manufacturability, and packaging compatibility
questions.explanation: Platform selection is a system tradeoff rather than a contest for the highest refractive index.

questions.prompt: What is heterogeneous integration in silicon photonics?
answers: Combining dissimilar materials, such as III-V gain material and silicon, on an integrated platform.
questions.explanation: Bonding or transfer printing can introduce capabilities absent from passive silicon.

questions.prompt: Select real constraints when moving a lab PIC to production.
options: A single successful die proves universal yield
Packaging can be ignored after tape-out
questions.explanation: Good nominal performance does not guarantee economical manufacturing.

questions.prompt: An optics PhD wants PIC design work. Name three concrete skills to demonstrate.
answers: Mode/device simulation; PDK-compliant layout; measurement-backed compact modeling.
questions.explanation: A reproducible portfolio should connect assumptions, fabricated geometry, and measured performance.

questions.prompt: Why are telecom wavelengths commonly used on silicon platforms?
answers: Silicon is relatively transparent there and mature fiber components exist
options: Silicon is relatively transparent there and mature fiber components exist
Visible light is always transparent in silicon
questions.explanation: Material absorption, detector availability, and the fiber ecosystem shape the operating band.

questions.prompt: Arrange a simplified fabless PIC development flow.
questions.explanation: Measurement closes the design loop; subsequent iterations update models and tolerances.

questions.prompt: Distinguish a demonstration bandwidth from a deployable product specification.
answers: A demo shows performance in stated conditions; a product needs corners, reliability, yield, and interfaces specified.
questions.explanation: Temperature, laser power, error rate, and packaging conditions must accompany headline bandwidth.

questions.prompt: At 1310 nm, the telecom band commonly called the ___ band is used.
questions.explanation: The O band is roughly 1260–1360 nm; the C band is around 1530–1565 nm.

questions.prompt: Prioritize a platform feasibility check before choosing a layout tool.
questions.explanation: Tool preference should follow process and product feasibility.

questions.prompt: Which quantity relates a guided mode propagation constant to free-space wavenumber?
questions.explanation: n_eff = beta/k0. It describes modal phase propagation, not simply the bulk silicon index.

questions.prompt: The propagation constant beta equals 2π n_eff divided by ___.
questions.explanation: Use the vacuum wavelength in this definition, not the already shortened guided wavelength.

questions.prompt: Distinguish effective index from group index.
answers: Effective index determines phase; group index determines group delay and spectral spacing.
questions.explanation: n_g = n_eff − λ dn_eff/dλ for the usual wavelength convention.

questions.prompt: What usually happens when a bend radius is made too small?
questions.explanation: A tightly curved mode can leak; transitions into the bend can add mismatch loss.

questions.prompt: Why do high-contrast waveguides need a vector mode solver?
answers: Longitudinal fields and polarization coupling can be significant; a scalar approximation may miss them.
questions.explanation: A rectangular high-contrast guide is not accurately described by a weak-guidance fiber formula alone.

questions.prompt: A rib waveguide retains a surrounding silicon ___.
questions.explanation: A partial etch leaves a slab; a fully etched strip has a different confinement and electrical design.

questions.prompt: Select causes of propagation loss in a passive fabricated waveguide.
questions.explanation: Bend radiation is another contribution when curved sections are present.

questions.prompt: Why is the label TE-like used on rectangular waveguides?
answers: The dominant electric field is transverse in the specified orientation, but the full mode is generally hybrid.
questions.explanation: Always define the coordinate convention rather than assuming a universal TE axis.

questions.prompt: A mode lies near cutoff. Which concern grows?
answers: Sensitivity to geometry and confinement leakage
options: Sensitivity to geometry and confinement leakage
questions.explanation: Near-cutoff modes can be weakly confined and highly sensitive to thickness or width changes.

questions.prompt: What should a mode-confinement factor state explicitly?
answers: Which field or power integral is used and which material region is integrated.
questions.explanation: Different definitions matter for gain overlap, absorption, and nonlinear calculations.

questions.prompt: Group velocity is c divided by the ___ index.
questions.explanation: This is the guided-mode group velocity in a suitable narrowband regime.

questions.prompt: For n_g = 4 and length 3 mm, what is the group delay? Use c = 3×10⁸ m/s.
How would you decide whether a guide is single-mode over a wavelength band?
answers: Solve supported modes across wavelength and process corners; inspect confinement, loss, and possible slab modes.
questions.explanation: A single nominal solver result does not establish broadband single-mode behavior.

questions.prompt: Select consequences of changing waveguide width.
questions.explanation: Width affects both phase and confinement, so a change can alter couplers and resonances too.

questions.prompt: Why can an Euler bend reduce transition loss relative to an abrupt circular bend?
answers: Its curvature changes gradually, reducing mismatch between straight and bent modes.
questions.explanation: A smooth curvature profile helps, but minimum radius and footprint still matter.

questions.prompt: At 2 dB/cm, what propagation loss comes from 5 mm of straight guide?
questions.explanation: Five millimeters is 0.5 cm; multiply length by loss per unit length.

questions.prompt: Arrange a waveguide mode-design workflow.
questions.explanation: Track mode identity rather than trusting solver mode numbers through crossings.

questions.prompt: Why can identical widths in two different stacks have different effective indices?
answers: Thickness, cladding, etch depth, material indices, and stress change the mode.
questions.explanation: Geometry alone is not a complete waveguide specification.

questions.prompt: Evanescent fields decay outside a guide but enable ___ between nearby guides.
questions.explanation: An evanescent tail allows energy transfer when nearby modes overlap.

questions.prompt: Arrange checks for a suspiciously low-loss simulated bend.
answers: Compare converged loss and mode profile
options: Compare converged loss and mode profile
questions.explanation: Tiny reported losses can reflect numerical limits rather than true device performance.

questions.prompt: How does a directional coupler transfer optical power?
answers: Through coupling of nearby waveguide modes
options: Through coupling of nearby waveguide modes
questions.explanation: Overlapping evanescent fields form supermodes with different propagation constants.

questions.prompt: For matched guides, coupled power often follows sin²(κ ___).
questions.explanation: κ is the amplitude coupling coefficient and L is interaction length in the ideal two-mode model.

questions.prompt: What sets the full-transfer length of a matched directional coupler?
answers: The even/odd supermode propagation-constant splitting; L_transfer = π/(beta_even − beta_odd).
questions.explanation: Equivalently, L_transfer = π/(2κ) under the conventional coupled-mode definition.

questions.prompt: An ideal 50:50 splitter sends what fraction of input power to each output?
questions.explanation: Each branch is about −3.01 dB relative to input; this is splitting, not excess loss.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish splitter imbalance from excess loss?
answers: Imbalance compares outputs; excess loss compares their summed power with input power.
questions.explanation: A lossless asymmetric splitter may be imbalanced without dissipating power.

questions.prompt: An MMI coupler uses multimode ___.
questions.explanation: Self-imaging in a multimode region creates useful splitting and combining patterns.

questions.prompt: Select specifications for a passive optical splitter.
questions.explanation: Bandwidth, polarization behavior, and fabrication tolerance are also important.

questions.prompt: Why does coupling gap variation matter strongly?
answers: Evanescent overlap changes rapidly with gap, altering the coupling coefficient and split ratio.
questions.explanation: Include lithographic and etch variation in coupler tolerance sweeps.

questions.prompt: What happens when guides in a directional coupler have a large phase mismatch?
questions.explanation: Detuning suppresses complete transfer even if the interaction length is increased.

questions.prompt: What is an adiabatic taper trying to preserve?
answers: The desired evolving local mode, with minimal conversion to unwanted modes or radiation.
questions.explanation: Slow geometry change is judged against local mode separation, not just absolute length.

questions.prompt: A Bragg grating creates wavelength-selective ___.
questions.explanation: A periodic perturbation phase-matches forward and backward propagation.

questions.prompt: For a first-order Bragg grating, n_eff = 2.5 and λ = 1550 nm. Approximate period?
questions.explanation: λ_B ≈ 2 n_eff Λ, so Λ ≈ 1550/5 nm.

questions.prompt: Why use a waveguide crossing design instead of intersecting narrow strips casually?
answers: An engineered crossing reduces radiation, unwanted coupling, and backreflection.
questions.explanation: Evaluate insertion loss and crosstalk for each crossing direction and polarization.

questions.prompt: Select properties of a reciprocal passive device without magneto-optic bias.
answers: Reciprocal port-to-port transmission under consistent normalization
No optical gain if all materials are passive
options: Reciprocal port-to-port transmission under consistent normalization
No optical gain if all materials are passive
questions.explanation: Reciprocity does not require a symmetric geometry or equal loss for different input modes.

questions.prompt: Can a reciprocal lossless three-port be perfectly matched at every port? Explain.
answers: Not in the usual single-mode reciprocal three-port network model.
questions.explanation: This limitation helps explain why a splitter model may include reflection or radiation channels.

questions.prompt: Which data best supports coherent circuit simulation of a coupler?
questions.explanation: Power-only data loses phase, which matters when paths later interfere.

questions.prompt: Arrange passive component model extraction.
questions.explanation: Account for the reference planes and wavelength interpolation.

questions.prompt: Why do port reference planes affect extracted phase?
answers: Moving a plane adds propagation phase and delay to its scattering coefficients.
questions.explanation: Models can be individually correct yet inconsistent when combined with overlapping access-waveguide lengths.

questions.prompt: An AWG separates wavelengths using a phased array of ___ with incremental lengths.
questions.explanation: The path-length increment creates wavelength-dependent interference at output ports.

questions.prompt: Arrange a robust splitter selection process.
questions.explanation: Compare at the same wavelength range and reference planes.

questions.prompt: What does an MZI convert into an output intensity change?
questions.explanation: Splitting and recombining creates interference controlled by the arm phase difference.

questions.prompt: At a constructive output of an ideal balanced MZI, T = cos²(Δφ/___).
questions.explanation: The complementary output follows sin²(Δφ/2), given consistent coupler phase conventions.

questions.prompt: Why is quadrature useful for analog MZI modulation?
answers: The intensity transfer function has a large approximately linear local slope.
questions.explanation: The linear region is limited; large signals introduce distortion.

questions.prompt: At Δφ = π, what is T = cos²(Δφ/2)?
questions.explanation: This specified output is dark; the ideal complementary port is bright.

questions.prompt: What limits extinction in a real MZI besides phase error?
answers: Splitter imbalance, unequal arm loss, polarization contamination, and stray background light.
questions.explanation: Perfect phase control cannot cancel unequal interfering amplitudes completely.

questions.prompt: Vπ is the voltage change producing a ___ phase shift under the stated drive convention.
questions.explanation: Single-arm and push-pull definitions must not be mixed.

questions.prompt: Select contributors to MZI phase drift.
options: The label on a measurement file
questions.explanation: A phase difference depends on both material and geometry.

questions.prompt: What is the wavelength FSR of an unequal-arm MZI approximately?
answers: FSR_λ ≈ λ²/(n_g ΔL), when dispersion is weak over one fringe.
questions.explanation: Use group index; effective index alone neglects wavelength dependence.

questions.prompt: At λ = 1550 nm, n_g = 4, and ΔL = 100 µm, approximate FSR?
questions.explanation: Using consistent micrometer units gives 1.55²/(4×100) µm = 0.006 µm.

questions.prompt: What does push-pull drive mean in an MZI?
answers: Drive the arms with opposite phase changes to increase differential phase and potentially reduce chirp.
questions.explanation: The voltage convention and phase-shifter symmetry determine the actual benefit.

questions.prompt: A phase shifter with smaller VπL has greater phase-shift ___ per length and voltage.
questions.explanation: VπL is useful but does not capture loss, capacitance, bandwidth, or drive power alone.

questions.prompt: An arm has Δn_eff = 0.001 over 775 µm at λ = 1550 nm. Phase change?
Why does a longer phase shifter not always make a better modulator?
answers: It lowers required voltage but can increase loss, capacitance, delay, and RF attenuation.
questions.explanation: Optimize a link-level objective rather than Vπ alone.

questions.prompt: Select quantities to record when reporting Vπ.
questions.explanation: Temperature and measurement frequency can matter as well.

questions.prompt: What does an MZI fringe measurement reveal about group index?
answers: With known differential length, fringe spacing estimates n_g.
questions.explanation: Calibration and dispersion affect the estimate; distinguish differential group delay from common delay.

questions.prompt: For ideal equal-amplitude arms, which phase difference gives quadrature?
questions.explanation: The intensity is half-scale with nonzero slope at these bias points.

questions.prompt: Arrange an MZI bias calibration.
questions.explanation: Drift requires monitoring rather than a one-time nominal setting.

questions.prompt: How can common-mode temperature shifts still change an unequal-arm MZI?
answers: Unequal optical lengths turn a common index shift into a differential phase shift.
questions.explanation: Balanced physical lengths also need matched thermo-optic responses to suppress drift.

questions.prompt: The extinction ratio in dB is 10 log10(P_max / ___).
questions.explanation: Use powers. An amplitude ratio would use 20 log10.

questions.prompt: Arrange troubleshooting for poor MZI extinction.
answers: Check splitter balance and arm loss
options: Check splitter balance and arm loss
questions.explanation: Separate measurement limits from device amplitude and phase errors.

questions.prompt: What sets a ring resonance?
answers: Round-trip phase is an integer multiple of 2π
options: Round-trip phase is an integer multiple of 2π
The ring is exactly one vacuum wavelength wide
questions.explanation: The circulating field returns in phase after a full round trip.

questions.prompt: The approximate frequency FSR is c divided by n_g times round-trip ___.
questions.explanation: The round-trip group delay sets the frequency spacing.

questions.prompt: Distinguish loaded Q and intrinsic Q.
answers: Intrinsic Q reflects internal loss; loaded Q also includes coupling loss to external ports.
questions.explanation: For one coupling channel, 1/Q_loaded = 1/Q_intrinsic + 1/Q_coupling.

questions.prompt: A resonance at 1550 nm has linewidth 0.155 nm. Approximate loaded Q?
questions.explanation: Q ≈ λ_res/Δλ for a narrow isolated resonance.

questions.prompt: What is critical coupling in a single-bus ring?
answers: External coupling loss equals internal round-trip loss, enabling a deep through-port notch in the ideal model.
questions.explanation: It is not equivalent to choosing a 50:50 directional coupler.

questions.prompt: If external coupling is weaker than intrinsic loss, a ring is ___.
questions.explanation: Overcoupling means stronger external coupling than internal loss.

questions.prompt: Select effects that can shift a ring resonance.
questions.explanation: All can change optical path length or effective index.

questions.prompt: Explain the high-Q bandwidth tradeoff for a ring modulator.
answers: Higher Q increases resonant enhancement but narrows optical bandwidth and lengthens photon lifetime.
questions.explanation: Electrical RC can provide an additional independent bandwidth limit.

questions.prompt: A ring has n_g = 4 and circumference 100 µm. Approximate frequency FSR?
Why can one notch-depth measurement fail to distinguish undercoupling from overcoupling?
answers: Intensity-only measurements can leave a coupling-regime ambiguity.
questions.explanation: Phase information or additional measurements can resolve the ambiguity.

questions.prompt: Heating a typical silicon ring near telecom wavelengths usually shifts resonance toward ___ wavelengths.
questions.explanation: Positive thermo-optic response usually causes a redshift; special compensated structures can behave differently.

questions.prompt: What does an add-drop ring provide that a single-bus ring lacks?
answers: A second waveguide port for dropping resonant light
options: A second waveguide port for dropping resonant light
An intrinsic laser in any material
questions.explanation: The second bus adds coupling and changes loaded Q and power distribution.

questions.prompt: Why do backscattering defects sometimes split a ring resonance?
answers: They couple clockwise and counterclockwise modes, creating distinct standing-wave resonances.
questions.explanation: A simple single-traveling-mode model may then be inadequate.

questions.prompt: Select requirements for a useful ring wavelength-lock loop.
options: Unbounded loop gain at all frequencies
questions.explanation: Noise, capture range, and thermal crosstalk affect locking.

questions.prompt: What does finesse compare?
answers: FSR to resonance linewidth, in the same frequency or wavelength units locally.
questions.explanation: Finesse and Q are related but not interchangeable; Q also includes the carrier frequency.

questions.prompt: If ring round-trip length doubles and n_g stays constant, frequency FSR does what?
questions.explanation: FSR is inversely proportional to round-trip length.

questions.prompt: Arrange a ring spectral characterization.
questions.explanation: Sampling must resolve the linewidth before a fit can be trusted.

questions.prompt: What information is needed to convert intrinsic Q into propagation loss?
answers: Group index and a clearly defined loss convention; alpha_power ≈ 2π n_g/(Q_i λ).
questions.explanation: This gives power attenuation in inverse length; convert separately into dB per length.

questions.prompt: For field decay rate and energy decay rate, a factor of ___ must be handled consistently.
questions.explanation: Optical energy is proportional to field amplitude squared.

questions.prompt: Arrange selecting a ring modulator for a link.
answers: Validate at electrical and optical corners
options: Validate at electrical and optical corners

questions.prompt: What does WDM add to an optical link?
answers: Multiple independently modulated wavelength channels share an optical path.
questions.explanation: Filtering, source stability, channel crosstalk, and power distribution add constraints.

questions.prompt: FEC stands for forward error ___.
questions.explanation: FEC adds redundancy and can improve error tolerance, with overhead and latency.

questions.prompt: Select contributors to a practical optical power budget.
questions.explanation: Connectors, distribution, and receiver interface losses can also matter.

questions.prompt: Why specify whether sensitivity is in average power or OMA?
answers: The conversion depends on extinction ratio and modulation format.
questions.explanation: Mixing conventions can create an apparently positive but invalid link margin.

questions.prompt: Tx = +3 dBm, total loss = 8 dB, Rx sensitivity = −10 dBm. Margin?
questions.explanation: Received power is −5 dBm; margin is −5 − (−10) = 5 dB.

questions.prompt: What does optical crosstalk do in WDM?
answers: Unwanted channel leakage degrades signal quality; effects depend on spectral overlap and coherence.
questions.explanation: A filter's nominal isolation must be checked across drift and process corners.

questions.prompt: At optical frequency f, a small wavelength change obeys Δf ≈ −c Δλ / ___.
questions.explanation: Frequency decreases as wavelength increases; use magnitudes for channel spacing.

questions.prompt: Near 1550 nm, 0.8 nm wavelength spacing is approximately what frequency spacing?
questions.explanation: c Δλ/λ² gives roughly 100×10⁹ Hz.

questions.prompt: Why compare total pJ/bit rather than only modulator switching energy?
answers: Source, drivers, TIAs, SerDes, DSP, tuning, and control can dominate system power.
questions.explanation: State whether total bandwidth is one-directional or bidirectional.

questions.prompt: Select benefits CPO can offer relative to long electrical traces to front-panel optics.
answers: Potential reduction in electrical I/O energy
options: Potential reduction in electrical I/O energy
Guaranteed field replacement of every engine
questions.explanation: Benefits depend on architecture and accounting; optical attachment and serviceability become harder.

questions.prompt: Distinguish scale-up and scale-out interconnect priorities.
answers: Scale-up tightly couples compute resources with strong bandwidth/latency demands; scale-out links larger distributed systems.
questions.explanation: Terminology and boundaries vary; understand the employer's actual topology.

questions.prompt: An optical subsystem uses 8 W and carries 2 Tb/s one-way aggregate data. Energy per bit?
questions.explanation: 8 J/s divided by 2×10¹² bits/s = 4×10⁻¹² J/bit.

questions.prompt: Arrange a link-level design workflow.
answers: Define reach, rate, and error target
options: Define reach, rate, and error target
questions.explanation: Include all reference-plane losses and overhead consistently.

questions.prompt: Why is Nyquist bandwidth not a guaranteed device bandwidth requirement?
answers: Pulse shaping, equalization, filter response, and implementation penalties determine the usable link.
questions.explanation: Avoid a universal bandwidth-to-bit-rate rule without waveform assumptions.

questions.prompt: OMA for binary optical levels is P1 ___ P0.
questions.explanation: OMA is a power difference; extinction ratio is a ratio.

questions.prompt: Arrange debugging a failing BER test.
answers: Verify clock, pattern, and receiver setup
Isolate wavelength, thermal, and crosstalk penalties
options: Verify clock, pattern, and receiver setup
Isolate wavelength, thermal, and crosstalk penalties
questions.explanation: Change one controlled variable at a time and preserve the baseline.

questions.prompt: What does co-packaged optics place close together?
answers: Optical engines and the compute or switch ASIC package
options: Optical engines and the compute or switch ASIC package
questions.explanation: The goal is short electrical reach, with optical attachment and thermal constraints.

questions.prompt: A known-good ___ is screened before costly assembly.
questions.explanation: Screening reduces the risk of packaging a bad component, though coverage is never perfect.

questions.prompt: Why is packaging central to silicon photonics economics?
answers: Fiber alignment, electrical attachment, thermal management, testing, and yield can dominate cost and complexity.
questions.explanation: A small cheap PIC can still require an expensive assembly.

questions.prompt: Why can flip-chip interconnects help high-speed PIC/EIC integration?
answers: Shorter electrical paths can reduce parasitics
options: Shorter electrical paths can reduce parasitics
They remove the need for grounding
questions.explanation: Bump design, return paths, assembly yield, and thermal stress still need validation.

questions.prompt: What is thermal crosstalk between heaters?
answers: Heating one device changes neighboring temperatures and optical states.
questions.explanation: Characterize the coupling matrix and transient response before designing controllers.

questions.prompt: CTE stands for coefficient of thermal ___.
questions.explanation: Mismatched expansion can cause stress and alignment shifts across temperature cycles.

questions.prompt: Select packaging reliability concerns.
questions.explanation: Bond and solder fatigue can be important as well.

questions.prompt: Why is fiber attachment often harder near a high-power ASIC?
answers: Space, heat, mechanical access, and routing constraints limit alignment and assembly choices.
questions.explanation: Consider optical access and cooling together early in floorplanning.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes active from passive optical alignment?
answers: Active alignment uses measured optical performance during positioning
options: Active alignment uses measured optical performance during positioning
Active alignment always uses a laser inside silicon
Active alignment means electrical contact only
questions.explanation: Passive alignment uses mechanical references without optimizing live transmission in the same way.

questions.prompt: Why include an optical power monitor in an engine?
answers: It supports source diagnostics, aging tracking, tuning, and fault detection.
questions.explanation: Monitor tap loss and calibration accuracy belong in the budget.

questions.prompt: Package signal integrity depends on a low-inductance current ___ path.
questions.explanation: Ground and return-path discontinuities can degrade RF performance despite a short signal trace.

questions.prompt: If three independent assembly steps each have 90% yield, combined yield is what?
questions.explanation: 0.9³ = 0.729; correlated failures require a more detailed model.

questions.prompt: Why is accelerated aging not a universal direct lifetime prediction?
answers: Extrapolation depends on the relevant failure mechanism and stress model.
questions.explanation: A different mechanism under extreme stress can invalidate the extrapolation.

questions.prompt: Select measurements for package qualification.
answers: Optical loss before and after stress
options: Optical loss before and after stress
questions.explanation: Qualification should reflect the actual mission profile.

questions.prompt: What tradeoff does an external serviceable laser introduce?
answers: It improves replacement/thermal separation but adds interfaces, distribution loss, and failure modes.
questions.explanation: Serviceability must be evaluated for the complete system.

questions.prompt: What is a useful reason for wafer-level optical testing?
answers: Screen devices and characterize variation before assembly
options: Screen devices and characterize variation before assembly
questions.explanation: Access structures and coupling strategy must support the test architecture.

questions.prompt: Arrange a simplified photonic assembly flow.
questions.explanation: The real sequence depends on process, cure temperatures, and mechanical access.

questions.prompt: Why consider test coverage when estimating final module yield?
answers: Unscreened failures pass into assembly; overly aggressive tests can reject good devices.
questions.explanation: Optimize defect detection, false rejects, test cost, and assembly value.

questions.prompt: Thermal resistance is commonly reported in kelvin per ___.
questions.explanation: ΔT ≈ R_th P for a suitable steady-state lumped approximation.

questions.prompt: Arrange diagnosing temperature-dependent package loss.
questions.explanation: A power drop can have optical, thermal, or mechanical causes.

questions.prompt: Which effect underlies an optical gyroscope's rotation measurement?
questions.explanation: Counterpropagating light acquires a rotation-dependent phase difference.

questions.prompt: A biosensor using a waveguide detects changes through its ___ field near the surface.
questions.explanation: Surface binding changes the local optical environment and can shift phase or resonance.

questions.prompt: Why does high refractive-index sensitivity not alone establish a good sensor?
answers: Noise, drift, specificity, functionalization, and calibration determine useful detection limits.
questions.explanation: Sensitivity and limit of detection are different metrics.

questions.prompt: What advantage can SiN offer for nonlinear photonics near 1550 nm?
answers: Low two-photon absorption relative to silicon in suitable stacks
options: Low two-photon absorption relative to silicon in suitable stacks
questions.explanation: Loss, dispersion, power handling, and material quality still matter.

questions.prompt: What is four-wave mixing?
answers: A third-order nonlinear interaction that exchanges energy among optical frequencies under appropriate phase matching.
questions.explanation: With a degenerate pump, signal and idler frequencies satisfy 2ω_p = ω_s + ω_i.

questions.prompt: Two-photon absorption in silicon generates free ___ that can add absorption.
questions.explanation: Carrier lifetime and extraction affect the resulting nonlinear loss and phase shift.

questions.prompt: Select prerequisites for efficient nonlinear frequency conversion.
questions.explanation: A resonator can enhance intensity but adds bandwidth and tuning constraints.

questions.prompt: Why is loss especially costly in single-photon photonic computing?
answers: Lost photons reduce success probabilities and create erasures or errors; multiple paths compound the loss.
questions.explanation: Quantum architectures need a full source, routing, switching, and detection budget.

questions.prompt: Which detector type can count individual telecom photons with high performance at cryogenic temperatures?
options: A ordinary power meter with no gain or time resolution
questions.explanation: SNSPDs trade strong performance for cryogenic and integration requirements.

questions.prompt: What does Hong–Ou–Mandel interference test?
answers: Indistinguishable photons entering a balanced beamsplitter show suppressed coincidence events.
questions.explanation: Visibility is affected by spectral, temporal, polarization, and multiphoton imperfections.

questions.prompt: A coherent LiDAR chirped-laser technique is commonly abbreviated ___.
questions.explanation: Frequency-modulated continuous-wave ranging uses a beat frequency; Doppler and chirp calibration matter.

questions.prompt: For a linear FMCW chirp, stationary-target beat frequency primarily scales with what?
questions.explanation: Distance follows from delay; target motion adds Doppler contributions.

questions.prompt: Why must a programmable photonic mesh be calibrated?
answers: Fabrication errors, drift, loss, and actuator crosstalk change its implemented transformation.
questions.explanation: Calibration should account for observability and phase ambiguities.

questions.prompt: Select credible portfolio evidence for a silicon photonics career transition.
answers: A measured or validated model with uncertainty
options: A measured or validated model with uncertainty
Only a headline bandwidth with no conditions
questions.explanation: These are proposed evidence items, not universal employer hiring requirements.

questions.prompt: How would you explain an optics PhD's fit for a characterization role?
answers: Connect optical metrology and physics to automated device tests, statistics, and model extraction; identify RF and process gaps.
questions.explanation: Use concrete transferable experiments rather than claiming the degree alone proves PIC experience.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish photonic compute from photonic interconnect startups?
answers: They optimize different workloads, metrics, and device/system constraints
options: They optimize different workloads, metrics, and device/system constraints
questions.explanation: Read the actual architecture and role instead of treating every photonics company as the same.

questions.prompt: Arrange a focused career-transition portfolio.
answers: Pick a target role and device problem
Build a reproducible design or test study
options: Pick a target role and device problem
Build a reproducible design or test study
questions.explanation: A small complete project can demonstrate more than a broad unvalidated concept.

questions.prompt: What should you extract when reading a photonics paper?
answers: Problem, platform, assumptions, metrics/reference planes, methods, limitations, and comparison conditions.
questions.explanation: Separate demonstrated measurements from simulation and future roadmap claims.

questions.prompt: A roadmap claim should be distinguished from a ___ result.
questions.explanation: Also distinguish simulation, prototype demos, and production-qualified specifications.

questions.prompt: Arrange evaluating a local job opportunity.
answers: Verify current employer and work location
options: Verify current employer and work location
questions.explanation: Company ownership and openings can change; use the live employer site.
